geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the generic lifted bar into a split-wing mass so the dominant form can articulate a clearer public seam and avoid the box-like reading.
Widen the inter-wing gap to strengthen the central void and make the section programmatically legible.
Preserve a ground connector so the figure remains one coherent mass with an active street threshold.
Orient the split along the long direction to maintain the bar-like dominant gesture.
Increase the court carve to improve publicness and reduce the perceived thickness of the mass.
Keep the courtyard aligned to the access side so the frontage response remains explicit.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the generic lift with a split-wing condition to strengthen the ground-threshold legibility and make the public void more spatially explicit while preserving the dominant bar.
Create a clearer separation between the two wing-like masses so the central void reads as usable public space rather than a shallow slit.
Keep a continuous ground-level connector to preserve the public threshold and prevent the split from fragmenting the mass.
Increase the carved public void so it becomes a more legible court/terrace figure with stronger neighborhood-public space value.
Maintain the access-aligned open side so the void continues to respond coherently to the verified road frontage.

rationale: The candidate reads as one clear elongated bar with a carved central slot/void and a lifted/connected upper condition, so the dominant gesture is legible across the four views. It responds reasonably to the parcel rather than just filling it, and the road frontage edge is met with a meaningful seam/void response rather than a sealed blank face. The main weakness is that the section is still somewhat box-like and the void is narrow, so the public-space figure is present but not yet fully civic or generous. However, the mass is coherent in all views and there is no visible collision across views, so it remains a plausible neighborhood-living early massing.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is simpler and more rectilinear; do not copy the curved roof/profile language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact low-rise mass with a carved central void and an upper bridge can create a legible public interior while keeping the ground edge active.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more expansive and multi-building; the candidate should remain a single dominant bar rather than a campus.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard-centered campus-like arrangement with stepped/terraced masses can support neighborhood-scale mixed program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference leans more open and transparent; the candidate is more enclosed and should keep the void readable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated mass with a central atrium-like void and a horizontally spread section fits neighborhood-commercial hybrid use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more sectional and landscape-integrated; the candidate lacks that richness but can borrow the terrace/bridge logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced horizontal massing with connected wings and a clear central open space can produce a calm but civic neighborhood figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference has more volumetric complexity and multiple wings; the candidate should avoid becoming fragmented.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking low-rise volumes and elevated connections can preserve a dominant courtyard while varying the upper mass.
